value.body: A precision agriculture engineer brings sensors, drones, GPS-guided machines and data tools to farming, so water, seed, fertiliser and sprays are applied where they are needed. Employers include agri-tech startups, drone service providers, irrigation and farm-equipment companies, and agri-input firms. Work mixes field visits and demonstrations with data analysis and product testing.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Tech Agricultural Engineering; GIS, remote-sensing or drone training helps

items.label: Common tools
items.value: GIS software, drone mapping apps, soil and weather sensors, spreadsheets

items.label: Drone operation
items.value: Flying a drone commercially needs a DGCA remote pilot certificate

items.label: Drones under the Namo Drone Didi scheme
items.note: For women's self-help groups to rent out to farmers, 2024-25 to 2025-26

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Graduates join agri-tech and drone companies as field or product engineers, often after projects in GIS, IoT or drones. A DGCA remote pilot certificate is useful where the role involves flying spray or survey drones.

value.title: At a glance
items: A newer field; many roles are with startups and can change quickly.
Next roles: product specialist, agronomy-data analyst, or operations lead.
Expect regular field travel to rural areas.
